course.title: Astronomical Instrumentation
course.description: Studies telescope optics, detectors, filters, spectrographs, adaptive optics, calibration systems, observatory operations, space-based instruments, error budgets, and instrument proposal design.

status.reviewStatus: Approved for review release; not yet approved for instructional use

cadence.rationale: Matched 1:1 biweekly cadence, following the ASTR230/ASTR310/ASTR330 precedent (a 3-credit, 14-lecture structure consistent with ASTR320's own matched-cadence 3-credit course), because ASTR340's seven thematic units each build one self-contained instrumentation skill (telescope optics/resolution, focal-plane geometry/detectors, noise/SNR, calibration/photometry, spectroscopy, adaptive optics/space instruments, error budgets) toward a single capstone (Lab/PS 07, an instrument-proposal synthesis). See syllabus.html Lecture, Lab, and Problem-Set Cadence.

dataProvenance.src: materials/ASTR340/src/generate_astr340_content.py and generate_astr340_labs_psets.py generate all worked examples, lecture slides/notes, labs, and problem sets programmatically from shared constants.
realData: Keck I/II telescope aperture, collecting area, effective focal length, segment count/width, altitude, and active-optics surface accuracy - live-verified via direct web fetch this session (Wikipedia "W. M. Keck Observatory", 2026-09-24).
Keck HIRES radial-velocity precision (1.0 m/s) and 1 AU planet-detection limit (0.2 Jupiter masses) - live-verified via the same web fetch this session, citing Vogt et al. (1994), SPIE 2198, 362.

HIRES resolving power, groove density, and blaze angle; HST, VLT, JWST aperture/focal-length specifications; DECam pixel format; e2v-class CCD quantum-efficiency curve; Johnson-Cousins UBVRI bandpasses (Bessell 1990); Landolt standard star SA 98-978 (Landolt 1992); Keck adaptive optics Strehl-ratio figures (Wizinowich et al. 2000) - standard published instrument/mission/facility specifications, not independently re-verified this session, flagged for spot-check in reference-log.md.

System throughput, sky brightness, HIRES beam width, and photometric error-budget terms - representative illustrative values, explicitly labeled as such in reference-log.md, distinct from the real-data provenance items above.
